english.html: last sigh of life, inasmuch as the manners and affections of men often change, whether through prosperity or through adversity, or through the heaviness of old age; and sometimes friendships part over contentions and quarrels, or over some good, profit and advantage to which each one pretends and aspires particularly for himself <sup class="mk" data-key="o">o</sup>. But that, for such a separation of friendship, people should afterwards come to disclose and reproach one another with the secret things they had previously communicated to each other — that, in my opinion, is done only among wretched and deplorable persons.

notes.gloss: Friendships change with fortune, age and rivalry for advantage.

english.html: The said du Tilh, trusting in the fact that he entirely bore the features and lineaments of the face of the said Martin, violating in the first place all laws of friendship, and afterwards using a new kind of effrontery and trickery, had presented himself to the four sisters, uncle and relatives of this Martin, and to the said Bertrande de Rols, indeed to all those of the place of Artigat: giving to all several particular and such close tokens, that not only the strangers, but also all the said relatives, indeed the supplicant, persuaded themselves that it was truly Martin Guerre.

This is, in its kind, the greatest, most prodigious and most marvellous deed that can be read of in any annals whatsoever, whether Greek or Latin, ancient or modern: in which one will indeed hear of several examples of certain persons so alike among themselves that those who saw them remained bewildered and confused, not knowing how to distinguish or recognise them, and often taking the one for the other; and that under the pretext of this re

uncertain.note: the marker after 'ſoy' and the key before the margin note are both printed as a solid round ink blob (body-2.jpg x~1650; margin-1.jpg x~90 y~740); reader A read e, reader B a. Keyed o from the sequence: the marker alphabet runs continuously through an annotation across pages (p002 a-f / p003 g-r; p005 a-f / p006 g-n; p009 a-d / p010 e-n) and this block ends the annotation whose last marker on p010 is {n}. The blob's closed round outline is consistent with o.

the last word is two over-inked strokes fused into one mass (margin-1.jpg x~375-410 y~730): a tall stroke and a short one, nothing printed to the right. Read 'li' (= livre, continued by 'de Amicitia.'); a point merged into the blob ('li.') cannot be excluded. A stray dot sits above the C of 'Cicero'.
the only margin note on the page; its first line stands beside blocks[0].lines[6], one line below the marker. margin-2/3/4.jpg are blank; no foot citations, signature or catchword.
